sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page 'Onin Pidgin' (onin1237) and reference record 57587
sources.note: Nothing; lists exactly one source (Donohue 1996, Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist). No grammar, sketch, phonology or wordlist of the pidgin exists in Glottolog. AES: extinct; Ethnologue comment 'Onin Based Pidgin (onx) = 9 (Second language only)'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Onin language' / 'Pidgin Onin' infobox; id.wikipedia 'Bahasa Onin'
sources.note: Nothing on stress; tertiary. Says only that Onin 'is the basis of a local pidgin' (citing Ethnologue onx) and that Onin has 18 consonants and 5 vowels (citing OLAC).

sources.citation: Iribaram. 2017. Pronomina bahasa Onin [Pronoun of Onin language]. Totobuang 4(2).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Kantor Bahasa (Papua) journal article on the lexifier Onin; Indonesian descriptive articles of this kind often open with a short phonology/stress note. Open-access PDF at totobuang.kemdikbud.go.id/jurnal/index.php/totobuang/article/download/26/20, but the host did not resolve by automated download.

sources.note: Phonology of the lexifier Onin (onin1245, ISO oni), the language the pidgin simplifies; most likely place for a stress rule of Onin proper, which would be the best proxy for the pidgin. Glottolog marks the file nosharefn; not found online.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 1996. Some trade languages of insular South-East Asia and Irian Jaya. In Wurm, Mühlhäusler & Tryon (eds.), Atlas of Languages of Intercultural Communication in the Pacific, Asia, and the Americas, II:2, 713-716. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.

sources.note: The only source Glottolog lists for the pidgin; seen only in Google Books snippets. Full pp. 714-715 would confirm it is silent on Onin Pidgin phonology (snippets show a sociolinguistic paragraph; the stress sentence is in the Tukang Besi section).

sources.citation: Coenen, J. 1954. [title not seen; cited by Donohue 1996: 715 for the origin of Onin as 'a mixture of the Kei languages and Iha']

sources.note: The only earlier primary source on Onin that Donohue cites; a missionary-era manuscript on the Onin peninsula languages may contain notes on Onin as a trade language. Title and location unknown; seen only as a citation in a snippet.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 page for the lexifier Onin (onin1245, ISO oni) with BibTeX for Muti 2013, Setyaningsih 2014, Modera 1830
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Shows that the LEXIFIER Onin has a phonology (Muti, Wa Ode 2013, 'Phonemic inventory of Onim language', MA thesis, Universitas Negeri Papua, Manokwari, xviii+91 pp., listed by Glottolog as a phonology, Glottolog nosharefn) — not online; nothing for the pidgin.

Live page 403; no archived copy at the Internet Archive exists (archive.org availability API returned none). Glottolog quotes its content: second-language-only pidgin, status 9/extinct — no linguistic description.
